'''Gregory Ross Stiemsma''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|s|t|iː|m|s|m|ə}}; born September 26, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who spent four seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played high school basketball for [[Randolph High School (Wisconsin)|Randolph High School]] and college basketball for the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], before going undrafted in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. A 6'11" [[Center (basketball)|center]], Stiemsma was known for his defense and shot blocking ability during his playing days.

==High school career==
Stiemsma attended [[Randolph High School (Wisconsin)|Randolph High School]] in [[Randolph, Wisconsin]] where he led the Rockets to Division 4 state titles as a sophomore, junior and senior.<ref>{{cite web | last=Cullen | first=Eric | url=http://badgerherald.com/sports/2004/03/22/stiemsmas-randolph-r/ | title=Stiemsma's Randolph Rockets secure 3rd-straight title | work=BadgerHerald.com | date=March 22, 2004 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref> As a junior in 2002–03, he earned first-team all-state honors after averaging 14.5 points, 8.3 rebounds, 5.5 blocks and 2.7 assists per game.<ref name="bio">{{Cite web |title=Greg Stiemsma {{!}} Men's Basketball Coach |url=https://uwbadgers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/greg-stiemsma/2416 |access-date=2025-03-06 |website=Wisconsin Badgers |language=en}}</ref>

In November 2003, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://badgerherald.com/sports/2003/11/13/badgers-score-3-fres/ | title=Badgers score 3 freshmen | work=BadgerHerald.com | date=November 13, 2003 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref>

As a senior in 2003–04, he was limited to just 18 games due to right knee injury but still managed to earn third-team Associated Press all-state honors after averaging 11.6 points, 8.3 rebounds and 4.1 blocks per game.<ref name="bio" />

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]], Stiemsma played just 10 games after missing the first six weeks of the season with a right foot injury. In those 10 games, he averaged just 1.1 points per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name=stats>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/greg-stiemsma-1.html |title=Greg Stiemsma Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=September 4, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150314012311/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/greg-stiemsma-1.html |archive-date=March 14, 2015 }}</ref>

In his sophomore season, he was again disrupted, managing just 16 games after he was deemed ineligible to play during the second semester due to poor grades. Stiemsma was later diagnosed with depression as a result of his poor academic performance.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.familyaware.org/family-profiles/1008-greg-stiemsma-age-26-nba-player-major-depression.html | title=Greg Stiemsma, age 26, NBA player, major depression | work=FamilyAware.org | access-date=September 4, 2014 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20140905061333/http://www.familyaware.org/family-profiles/1008-greg-stiemsma-age-26-nba-player-major-depression.html | archive-date=September 5, 2014 | url-status=dead }}</ref> Despite this, he still finished the season first on the team in total blocks with 24. In those 16 games, he averaged 2.8 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.5 blocks per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his junior season, he played out his first full season, playing 34 of the 36 games while averaging 2.2 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his senior season, led the team with 40 blocks, while recording four double-digit scoring performances, including a career-high 14 points in the NCAA tournament against Kansas State. In 35 games, he averaged 3.5 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.1 blocks per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

==Professional career==

===Early years (2008–2011)===

====2008–09 season====
Stiemsma went undrafted in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. In August 2008, he signed with [[Oyak Renault]] of Turkey for the 2008–09 season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/081508aaa.html | archive-url=https://archive.today/20140905061333/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/081508aaa.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 5, 2014 | title=Stiemsma to play pro ball in Turkey | work=uwbadgers.com | date=August 15, 2008 | access-date=September 4, 2014 }}</ref> In February 2009, he left Oyak and signed with the [[Seoul SK Knights]] of South Korea for the rest of the season. On April 11, 2009, he was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA Development League]].

====2009–10 season====
In July 2009, Stiemsma joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the 2009 NBA Summer League. On November 1, 2009, he was reacquired by the Sioux Falls Skyforce. On April 13, 2010, he signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Wolves_Sign_Greg_Stiemsma_2010_04_13.html | title=Wolves Sign Greg Stiemsma | work=NBA.com | date=April 13, 2010 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref>

====2010–11 season====
In July 2010, Stiemsma joined the Minnesota Timberwolves for the 2010 NBA Summer League. On September 10, 2010, he was waived by the Timberwolves before appearing in a game for them.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=6496 | title=Timberwolves waive Greg Stiemsma | work=InsideHoops.com | date=September 10, 2010 | access-date=September 4, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316214411/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=6496 | archive-date=March 16, 2018 | url-status=dead }}</ref> Later that month, he signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/training_camp_roster_100925.html | title=Cavaliers Announce 2010-11 Training Camp Roster | work=NBA.com | date=September 25, 2010 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Cavaliers on October 2, 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/stiemsma_waived_101002.html | title=Cavaliers Waive Stiemsma | work=NBA.com | date=October 2, 2010 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref> Three days later, he signed a two-year deal with [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://mlbb.d11.gr/feed-items/turkey-turk-telekom-inks-big-guy-greg-stiemsma | title=Turkey - Turk Telekom inks big guy Greg Stiemsma | work=mlbb.gr | date=October 5, 2010 | access-date=September 4, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304111902/http://mlbb.d11.gr/feed-items/turkey-turk-telekom-inks-big-guy-greg-stiemsma | archive-date=March 4, 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

====2011–12 season====
On August 21, 2011, Stiemsma signed with [[BC Sokhumi]] of the [[Georgian Superliga]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/other-leagues/88167/shot-blocker-greg-stiemsma-inks-with-shokhumi-tbilisi.html | title=Shot blocker Greg Stiemsma inks with Shokhumi Tbilisi | work=Sportando.com | date=August 21, 2011 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref> but left before appearing in a game for them. On November 2, 2011, he was reacquired by the Sioux Falls Skyforce.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/siouxfalls/1112_training_camp_invitees_111102.html | title=Skyforce Announces 2011-12 Training Camp Invitees | work=NBA.com | date=November 2, 2011 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2011–2012)===
[[File:Greg Stiemsma warms up.jpg|thumb|right|Stiemsma with the Boston Celtics]]
On December 9, 2011, Stiemsma signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press120911-celtics-sign-stiemsma.html | title=Celtics Sign Greg Stiemsma | work=NBA.com | date=December 9, 2011 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref> On December 28, 2011, he made his NBA debut, recording 2 points, 6 blocks and 4 rebounds in a 78–97 loss to the New Orleans Hornets.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/games/20111228/BOSNOH/gameinfo.html | title=Notebook: Hornets 97, Celtics 78 | work=NBA.com | date=December 28, 2011 | access-date=September 4, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107185856/http://www.nba.com/games/20111228/BOSNOH/gameinfo.html | archive-date=January 7, 2012 | url-status=dead }}</ref> In March 2012, he signed a sponsorship deal with [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Camerato | first=Jessica | url=https://www.csnne.com/blog/celtics-talk/stiemsma-signs-nike | title=Stiemsma signs with Nike | work=CSNNE.com | date=March 29, 2012 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref>

On June 29, 2012, the Celtics extended a $1.05 million qualifying offer to Stiemsma, thereby making him a restricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web | last=Forsberg | first=Chris | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4695722/cs-extend-qualifying-offer-to-stiemsma | title=C's extend qualifying offer to Stiemsma | work=ESPN.com | date=June 29, 2012 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2012–2013)===
On July 21, 2012, Stiemsma received an offer sheet from the Minnesota Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.masslive.com/celtics/index.ssf/2012/07/minnesota_timberwolves_sign_bo.html | title=Minnesota Timberwolves sign Boston Celtics RFA Greg Stiemsma to offer sheet | work=MassLive.com | date=July 21, 2012 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref> Two days later, the Celtics withdrew their qualifying offer to Stiemsma, clearing the way for the Timberwolves to sign him as an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.twincities.com/ci_21140224/greg-stiemsma-clear-sign-timberwolves-after-celtics-withdraw | title=Greg Stiemsma clear to sign with Timberwolves after Celtics withdraw offer | work=TwinCities.com | date=July 23, 2012 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref> On August 2, 2012, he officially signed with the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-sign-free-agent-center-greg-stiemsma | title=Wolves Sign Free Agent Center Greg Stiemsma | work=NBA.com | date=August 2, 2012 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref>

On July 7, 2013, he was waived by the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-waive-greg-stiemsma-and-mickael-gelabale | title=Timberwolves Waive Greg Stiemsma and Mickael Gelabale | work=NBA.com | date=July 7, 2013 | access-date=September 4, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928233157/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-waive-greg-stiemsma-and-mickael-gelabale | archive-date=September 28, 2013 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2013–2014)===
On July 10, 2013, Stiemsma signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-greg-stiemsma | title=PELICANS SIGN GREG STIEMSMA | work=NBA.com | date=July 10, 2013 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref> On April 14, 2014, he was waived by the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-ely | title=PELICANS SIGN ELY; New Orleans Waives Stiemsma | work=NBA.com | date=April 14, 2014 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2014–2015)===
On September 4, 2014, Stiemsma signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/stiemsma_090414 | title=Raptors Sign Greg Stiemsma | work=NBA.com | date=September 4, 2014 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref>

On September 24, 2015, Stiemsma signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Magic Sign Four Free Agents To Round Out Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-four-free-agents-round-out-training-camp-roster|access-date=September 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2015}}</ref> However, due to an Achilles' tendon strain, Stiemsma was prevented from playing early in the preseason, appearing in a total of two exhibition games for the Magic, collecting 1.5 rebounds in 8.3 minutes per game. He was subsequently waived by the Magic on October 22 prior to the start of the regular season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Magic Waive Greg Stiemsma|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-waive-greg-stiemsma|access-date=October 22, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Orlando Magic waive Greg Stiemsma, leaving roster at 15 players for now|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/magic-basketblog/os-mbb-orlando-magic-waive-greg-stiemsma-20151022-post.html|access-date=October 22, 2015|work=OrlandoSentinel.com|date=October 22, 2015}}</ref>

On September 12, 2016, Stiemsma signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-greg-stiemsma|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN GREG STIEMSMA|work=NBA.com|date=September 12, 2016|access-date=September 12, 2016}}</ref> but was waived on October 21 after appearing in four preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-waive-grant-jerrett-and-greg-stiemsma|title=TRAIL BLAZERS WAIVE GRANT JERRETT AND GREG STIEMSMA|work=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
===Minnesota Timberwolves (2019–2021)===
On September 12, 2019, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] announced that they had named Stiemsma as player development associate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-finalize-coaching-staff|title=MINNESOTA TIMBERWOLVES FINALIZE COACHING STAFF|date=September 12, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 12, 2019}}</ref>

=== San Antonio Spurs (2021–2024) ===
Stiemsma worked as a video assistant in the film room with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in 2021. He was part of their 2022 Summer League coaching staff and later received a promotion in Player Development.<ref>{{cite web |title=SAN ANTONIO SPURS ANNOUNCE BASKETBALL OPERATIONS ADDITIONS AND PROMOTIONS |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/san-antonio-spurs-announce-basketball-operations-additions-and-promotions |website=NBA.com |date=September 23, 2022 |access-date=June 26, 2024}}</ref>

=== Wisconsin Badgers (2024–present) ===
Stiemsma was hired as the Director of Player Development for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badger's men's basketball team]] in July 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Greg Stiemsma {{!}} Men's Basketball Coach |url=https://uwbadgers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/greg-stiemsma/2416 |access-date=2025-03-06 |website=Wisconsin Badgers |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
In 2011, Stiemsma earned a bronze medal with [[United States men's national basketball team#Pan American Games|Team USA]] at the [[Pan American Games]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://usagym.org/pages/post.html?PostID=8993 | title=U.S. Men Win Team Bronze Medal At 2011 Pan Am Games | work=usagym.org | date=October 25, 2011 | access-date=September 4, 2014 | archive-date=September 6, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140906042332/https://usagym.org/pages/post.html?PostID=8993 | url-status=dead }}</ref> where he led the tournament in field goal percentage (.889) and was second in the tournament in blocked shots with 11.<ref>{{cite web | last=Sannicandro | first=Nick | url=http://clnsradio.com/boston-redsox-news/item/3073-99full-stiem-ahead-celtics-rookie-stiemsma-recognizes-dream | title=Full Stiem Ahead: Celtics Rookie Stiemsma Recognizes Dream | work=clnsradio.com | date=January 6, 2012 | access-date=September 4, 2014 | archive-date=September 6, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140906043458/http://clnsradio.com/boston-redsox-news/item/3073-99full-stiem-ahead-celtics-rookie-stiemsma-recognizes-dream | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Stiemsma is the son of Rick and Sharry Stiemsma, and has one sister, Erin. He and his wife Emily have two daughters and one son together.<ref name="bio" /> He is of [[Dutch people|Dutch]] origin.<ref>{{cite web | last=Doyle | first=Bill | url=http://www.telegram.com/article/20120108/COLUMN08/101089930/1009 | title=NBA: Boston Celtics' Greg Stiemsma can block with best | work=Telegram.com | date=January 8, 2012 | access-date=September 4, 2014}}</ref> He has admitted to suffering from [[Depression (mood)|depression]].<ref>[https://familyaware.org/greg-stiemsma/ Greg Stiemsma]</ref>
